text: In this video, we'll install OpenCrabs on Ubuntu, from zero to your first chat. It takes about five minutes.
You need Ubuntu 24.04 or newer on a 64-bit machine, an internet connection, and a key or subscription from an AI provider.
Open a terminal. On the Ubuntu desktop, press Control, Alt and T.
First, two quick checks. Your CPU type decides which file you download.
x86_64 means you want the amd64 download. On an ARM machine you'll see aarch64 instead, and you want arm64.
Next, your glibc version. It must be 2.39 or newer.
Here it says 2.39, so we're good. Older than that? This download won't run there, so watch the older systems video instead.
Now install three small helpers. curl downloads files, jq reads the release info, and libgomp is a library OpenCrabs needs to run.
Ubuntu asks for your password. Nothing appears while you type it. That's normal. Type it and press Enter.
Ubuntu fetches the package lists, then installs the helpers.
When you're back at the prompt, the helpers are ready.
Next, ask GitHub for the newest release, and keep its version number in a variable called TAG.
Print it to check. If you see a version number, like v0.5.4, you're good.
If the line comes back empty, just run the TAG command again before you move on.
Now download and unpack it in one line. The TAG variable fills in the version for you.
List the folder. You get two files: opencrabs itself, and rtk, a small helper it ships with.
On an ARM machine, the one that said aarch64, swap amd64 for arm64 in the file name.
This step is optional, but it's a good habit. Download the archive and the published list of checksums.
Then let sha256sum compare them. OK means your file is exactly what was released.
Unpack this checked copy, and you're set.
Now move both files into a folder on your path, so you can run OpenCrabs from anywhere. No sudo needed.
Check that it works.
If your terminal says command not found, open a new terminal window and try again. Still not found? Run this export line, then try once more.
Time for the first run. Type opencrabs and press Enter.
The setup wizard opens. Choose QuickStart, the sensible defaults, and press Enter.

Home Base is the dot opencrabs folder in your home directory. That's always the default. Keep Seed template files ticked. Those files give your crab its personality, and you can change them later. Press Enter.
Brain Fuel is the important one. Pick your AI provider. We'll choose Anthropic.
Now paste your API key, or a setup token if you have a Claude subscription. It's hidden on screen. Never share your key with anyone.
Keep the default model, or pick another one, and press Enter.
Always On can keep OpenCrabs running in the background. Skip it for now. There's a separate video for that.
Vibe Check makes sure everything is wired up. All OK? Press Enter.
Make It Yours lets you tell OpenCrabs about yourself. Press Escape to skip it for now.
Setup complete. And you're in. Say hi.
It answers. Your reply will be different, but that's it. OpenCrabs is installed and running.
If something goes wrong, here are the three errors people hit most, and the fix for each.
GLIBC 2.39 not found means your system is too old for this download. Watch the older systems video instead.
libgomp.so.1, cannot open shared object file, means the helpers are missing. Go back to chapter two.
gzip, unexpected end of file, means TAG was empty. Run chapter three again, then download again.
Every command from this video is in the description, ready to copy.
Next up: keep OpenCrabs running in the background, and connect it to Telegram so you can chat from your phone. See you there.
